Subject: Helio MSA redline (governing law + injunctive relief)

Vivek — attaching Helio's consolidated redline to the MSA (see Helio_MSA_redline_v2.docx). Two things driving the ask: (1) corporate counsel wants Delaware law for interpretation but will only accept arbitration in limited circumstances, and (2) they need a clear carveout for injunctive/equitable relief and a quick procedure for emergency relief.

High level asks from Helio counsel:
- Governing law: Delaware (we're open to CA choice if Redwood can accept injunctive carveouts)
- Arbitration: prefer it for disputes under $1M, but insist that preliminary injunctive relief and intellectual property preservation remain in court
- Venue: prefer SF or Delaware depending on which law is chosen

Can your team review the attached and confirm Redwood's tolerance for split jurisdiction (arbitration + court carveouts) and any SLA/ops impacts for emergency relief handling? We also need timing for an internal legal call — ideally tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks,
Sara

Sara — thanks for the redline. Quick confirmation: thread will stay in my mailbox; looping in Laura (contracts) and Kim (legal) for final position.

Two operational points from my side before legal deep-dive:
- Emergency relief requests: we need a documented triage and contact path (on-call for dev/infra + legal + account ops). If Helio wants court-based injunctive carveouts, we'll require an SLA exception and a dedicated escalation contact to avoid disruption to other tenants.
- Governing law split (Delaware for interpretation, court for injunctive relief) is workable in principle, but we should limit the carveout language to narrowly defined provisional measures to avoid broad forum-shopping.

Laura / Kim — can you confirm Redwood's legal position on: (a) accepting Delaware choice of law with court injunctive carveout, (b) whether we require a cap or notice period for emergency relief actions, and (c) any operational constraints (SLA exceptions, preserved logs) we should surface to Helio?

I'll propose a 40-minute slot tomorrow 9:30–10:10 PT unless legal needs longer.

— Vivek

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Sara Kim <sara.kim@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio MSA redline (governing law + injunctive relief)

Vivek / team / Sara — thanks for sending. I reviewed Helio's redline and attached a short position memo (Redwood_GoverningLaw_20260809.pdf attached). TL;DR: we can accommodate a split approach with the following guardrails that balance Helio's ask and Redwood's operational risk. Key points: 

1) Governing law: Accept Delaware substantive law for contract interpretation. Keep choice explicit and mutual.
2) Arbitration: Agree arbitration as primary forum for most disputes, but carve out provisional equitable relief (temporary restraining orders, injunctive relief to preserve IP/confidential data) to be available in court without prejudice to arbitration. Limit carveout scope to "provisional measures" and require prompt referral back to arbitration for the merits.
3) Venue: If Delaware law is chosen, allow either (a) Delaware courts for injunctive relief or (b) Northern District of California for urgent relief where injunctive performance is sought in CA. For ops simplicity, prefer one designated emergency forum per customer; if Helio wants flexibility between CA/DE we require additional notice and a short consent procedure.
4) Notice & escalation: For any emergency relief request Redwood requires 48 hours' notice where feasible, a named legal contact, and an on-call pager for infra during the first 24 hours of any preservation order. If immediate emergency court filings are required, Redwood reserves the right to request expedited meet-and-confer where practicable.
5) SLA exception & logging: Accept an SLA exception for injunctive relief cases on a case-by-case basis. We will require retention of relevant logs for at least 90 days and a limited scope of data export.
6) Cost allocation: Helio to cover reasonable incremental costs associated with expedited preservation / third-party subpoenas (standard carve language provided).

Actionables:
- I'll attach a marked MSA (small edits) and propose redline language for the "Provisional Relief" clause.
- Ben: please confirm whether Dedicated or Hosted customers should have different default language for emergency access.
- Vivek: please confirm if Redwood is prepared to sign a short SOW-style annex to document on-call contacts and contact SLAs if Helio needs that.

Sara — if that framework looks acceptable we can produce a clean redline + short annex and take a 30–40 min legal ops call tomorrow. Proposed times: 9:30–10:10 PT or 3:00–3:40 PT.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura / Vivek — thanks for the quick review and the practical guardrails. Jane and I reviewed the memo and Helio is comfortable with the provisional-measures carveout (limited to TROs and temporary injunctions) so long as Redwood commits to the 48-hour notice framework and provides the annex with on-call contacts.

Next steps from Helio:
- We'll accept Delaware governing law with the narrow provisional-relief carveout as proposed.
- Jane will upload a small set of counter-edits to your attached MSA redline tonight and we'll try to meet tomorrow 9:30 PT. Can you please send the annex template and the marked MSA before EOD?

Appreciate the cadence — Sara
